topics.topic: RuntimeEnvironment and run-settings identity, kind, minting authority, and identity source
questions: If `RuntimeEnvironment` is a runtime model, is it a value or entity, who mints it, and exactly what source establishes its identity?

If `RuntimeEnvironment` reaches State 6 as a runtime model, declare its permitted `kind` or its value/entity identity in State 1; otherwise remove the claim that model closure gives it fields or members.
What identity does `RuntimeEnvironment` have, given that the changed passage introduces it but sends its decision to A8 and State 6?

Who creates `RuntimeEnvironment` and the run-settings value, and are they minted directly from raw process-environment values, from an installation-kind value plus defaults, or by an external composition boundary?

The passage must either declare `RuntimeEnvironment` and any run-settings runtime model with the required identity, declare an applicable registered `kind`, or establish that they are not runtime models and will not receive runtime-model closure records.
If either item becomes a runtime model in State 6, is its identity value or entity, who mints it, and is it minted from raw environment values, installation defaults, or the resolved combination?

quotes:
Each run setting is a row of the start-up table that only the runtime settings module of SPEC_STANDARD 6.11
reads, into a field of the settings object; that module decides how a value is read.

| `environment` | `RuntimeEnvironment` | `PORTAL_DELIVERER_ENVIRONMENT` | required: the DEVELOPMENT, TEST or PRODUCTION member of = models.RuntimeEnvironment (values `development`, `test`, `production`) |
judgement.why: The later texts make RuntimeEnvironment a closed member-valued field of the settings object and assign reading that object from the process environment to the runtime-settings operation; State 1 expressly excludes this startup configuration from its own models, so its runtime-model identity rule does not apply here.

topics.topic: The complete run-settings inventory and the decisions supplied by A8
questions: Which named run-setting types or records does this passage refer to, and are any of them runtime models that require State 1 meanings and identities or State 6 contract_only justification?
What exact decisions does A8 supply for the run settings and `RuntimeEnvironment`, and what accepted text contains those decisions, since no A8 passage or result is provided here?
What run-setting facts does A8 supposedly decide, and what is the complete set of run settings whose meanings and optionality must be fixed before State 1 closes?

quotes:
Each run setting is a row of the start-up table that only the runtime settings module of SPEC_STANDARD 6.11
reads, into a field of the settings object; that module decides how a value is read. A required setting that
is absent ends the start, and an optional one that is absent takes its default. `environment` chooses which
default applies; the defaults of this table are the same for every member of = models.RuntimeEnvironment.
The port is a whole number from 1 to 65535, and a time zone the time zone database does not know ends the
start:

| Field | Type | Environment variable | Decided |
|---|---|---|---|
| `timezone` | `str` | `PORTAL_DELIVERER_TIMEZONE` | optional, `Europe/Madrid` when absent |
| `binary_root` | `str` | `PORTAL_DELIVERER_BINARY_ROOT` | required, per installation |
| `state_dir` | `str` | `PORTAL_DELIVERER_STATE_DIR` | required, per installation |
| `connections_file` | `str` | `PORTAL_DELIVERER_CONNECTIONS_FILE` | required, per installation |
| `credential_file` | `str` | `PORTAL_DELIVERER_CREDENTIAL_FILE` | required, per installation |
| `environment` | `RuntimeEnvironment` | `PORTAL_DELIVERER_ENVIRONMENT` | required: the DEVELOPMENT, TEST or PRODUCTION member of = models.RuntimeEnvironment (values `development`, `test`, `production`) |
| `port` | `int` | `PORTAL_DELIVERER_PORT` | optional, 8850 when absent |
judgement.why: A8's later accepted text provides the complete run-setting inventory, types, environment-variable sources, requiredness, defaults, validation facts, and RuntimeEnvironment members.

topics.topic: The complete typed fields or enum members and meanings of the runtime configuration models
questions: What are the closed fields or members of `RuntimeEnvironment`, rather than leaving State 6 to choose them?
Replace the deferral with the complete typed fields in State 1 if these are models, or state consistently that they are not models and will not receive model-closure fields or members.

The passage must either declare every field of each runtime model with its type in State 1, or state unambiguously that these are not models and remove the promise that model closure will supply their fields later.
What installation kinds are members of RuntimeEnvironment, and what does each member mean?

quotes:
Each run setting is a row of the start-up table that only the runtime settings module of SPEC_STANDARD 6.11
reads, into a field of the settings object; that module decides how a value is read.

| Field | Type | Environment variable | Decided |
|---|---|---|---|
| `timezone` | `str` | `PORTAL_DELIVERER_TIMEZONE` | optional, `Europe/Madrid` when absent |
| `binary_root` | `str` | `PORTAL_DELIVERER_BINARY_ROOT` | required, per installation |
| `state_dir` | `str` | `PORTAL_DELIVERER_STATE_DIR` | required, per installation |
| `connections_file` | `str` | `PORTAL_DELIVERER_CONNECTIONS_FILE` | required, per installation |
| `credential_file` | `str` | `PORTAL_DELIVERER_CREDENTIAL_FILE` | required, per installation |
| `environment` | `RuntimeEnvironment` | `PORTAL_DELIVERER_ENVIRONMENT` | required: the DEVELOPMENT, TEST or PRODUCTION member of = models.RuntimeEnvironment (values `development`, `test`, `production`) |
| `port` | `int` | `PORTAL_DELIVERER_PORT` | optional, 8850 when absent |
judgement.why: The later A8 text closes every settings-object field with its type and closes RuntimeEnvironment to DEVELOPMENT, TEST, and PRODUCTION with their serialized values.

topics.topic: Whether RuntimeEnvironment and run settings are runtime models or non-model startup configuration
questions: Is `RuntimeEnvironment` a runtime model whose meaning and identity must be decided in State 1, a justified contract_only runtime model introduced by contracts, or non-model startup configuration that must not receive a State 6 model-closure record?

Are the run settings and `RuntimeEnvironment` models whose meaning and identity State 1 must decide, or non-model configuration owned entirely by A8; and if they are non-model configuration, why does State 6 give them model-closure fields and members?

Are the run settings and RuntimeEnvironment typed runtime models that must receive State 1 meanings and identities, or non-model startup inputs; if they are non-models, under which stated model-closure category can State 6 give them fields and members?

quotes:
The run settings and `RuntimeEnvironment`, the kind of installation that chooses the defaults of the optional
run settings, are startup configuration read from the environment of the process, not models of this state.
A8 decides them, and the State 6 model closure gives their fields and members.
judgement.why: The passage explicitly classifies both items as startup configuration rather than State 1 models and assigns their structural closure to State 6, so mentioning later fields or members is not a conflicting State 1 classification.

topics.topic: The conceptual relationship between RuntimeEnvironment and run settings
questions: Is `RuntimeEnvironment` an enum-like installation kind, a product model containing run settings, or a separate value referenced by a run-settings model?

quotes:
Each run setting is a row of the start-up table that only the runtime settings module of SPEC_STANDARD 6.11
reads, into a field of the settings object; that module decides how a value is read.

| `environment` | `RuntimeEnvironment` | `PORTAL_DELIVERER_ENVIRONMENT` | required: the DEVELOPMENT, TEST or PRODUCTION member of = models.RuntimeEnvironment (values `development`, `test`, `production`) |
judgement.why: The later text makes RuntimeEnvironment the typed environment field within the settings object, rather than the settings object itself or a separate referenced settings entity.

topics.topic: The lifetime and replacement policy of the runtime configuration
questions: Is the configuration minted once for the lifetime of a process, recreated for each product action, or replaceable when the process environment or installation configuration changes?

quotes: Calls `public_op:runtime_settings.load_runtime_settings`, `public_op:deliverer_service.load_config`, `public_op:deliverer_service.read_token` and `public_op:deliverer_router.create_app` in that order, then serves the surface on the loopback interface and the `port` of the run settings until it is stopped.
judgement.why: The run-service operation loads the settings once during startup and then serves with those settings until stopped, so an environment change is not observed by each subsequent product action.

topics.topic: Whether resolved defaults or absence are stored in startup configuration
questions: When an optional run setting is absent, is its chosen default a fact stored in the startup configuration model, or does the model preserve absence and leave each product action to obtain the installation default?

quotes:
Each run setting is a row of the start-up table that only the runtime settings module of SPEC_STANDARD 6.11
reads, into a field of the settings object; that module decides how a value is read. A required setting that
is absent ends the start, and an optional one that is absent takes its default. `environment` chooses which
default applies; the defaults of this table are the same for every member of = models.RuntimeEnvironment.
judgement.why: The later rule says an absent optional setting takes its default while being read into a settings-object field, so product actions receive the resolved value rather than preserved absence.

topics.topic: Whether run settings form one model, several models, or unmodeled scalar inputs
questions: Do the run settings collectively form one typed model, exist as separate typed models, or remain unmodeled scalar inputs?

quotes:
- the type of the run settings, and `DeliveryContext`, the context of the operations that `deliverer_service` builds from them:
  binary store, state folder, time zone and connections file;
judgement.why: The later module text names one RuntimeSettings type owned by domain_models and imported by runtime_settings, so the settings form one typed model rather than several models or unmodeled scalar inputs.
